chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hamzah ibn Bazie, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'My Lord commanded me with being polite with the people just as He commanded with the fulfilment of the Obligations'.

key_terms.مُدَارَاة: Politeness, gentleness, or courteous dealing with people

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic concept of mudarāh mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish 'mudarāh' not merely as social etiquette but as a divine imperative on par with obligatory worship (farā'id). This equates the spiritual weight of interpersonal gentleness with ritual duties, reflecting the Shia emphasis on character (akhlaq) as integral to faith. The narration underscores that just as one must fulfill prayers and fasting, one must equally maintain harmonious relations with the community.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Commanded me with being polite with the people just as He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Commanded with the fulfilment of the Obligations’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from ibn Bazi’ from Hamza ibn Bazi’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘My Lord (Allah) has commanded me to be gentle to people just as He has commanded me to fulfill my obligations.’”
